facts.statement: The study found six new genetic changes in the PRR12 gene in unrelated people with intellectual disability, a pattern that was statistically significant.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers used mice and human stem cells grown into brain-like tissue to investigate how the gene works.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Having only one working copy of the PRR12 gene was found to hinder the development of brain cells and the growth of their connections, which is linked to cognitive problems.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The PRR12 protein was shown to be present at the control regions of important genes that manage brain cell growth and communication, such as SNCG.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Reducing the activity of the SNCG gene fixed the structural problems in the brain cells, which points to a possible treatment for children with this condition.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue
